evals.prompt: I'm the DevRel lead at Quillbridge - we make a Python SDK for warehouse ingestion, tag [quillbridge] on Stack Overflow: 1,412 questions, 338 with no answer at all, the oldest unanswered one is from 2019. Goal is fewer support tickets. My Q1 plan: we've created a 'QuillbridgeSupport' account that our 4 support engineers share on rotation (3 hours a week each), we work through the unanswered list oldest to newest so nothing gets left behind, each answer gets drafted by our internal LLM assistant from the docs and an engineer checks it before it goes up, and I'll ask the wider eng team (about 25 people with SO accounts) to upvote our answers so they sit above the stale ones. The profile bio already says 'Quillbridge team' so disclosure is handled. We want the backlog gone in 8 weeks. Turn this into a week-by-week plan.
evals.expected_output: A reply that refuses the shared account, the LLM drafting, the upvote drive and profile-only disclosure, restates the goal as owning the high-view threads, picks the Curate posture with its predicate, triages the backlog by views and root cause into canonicals plus duplicate flags, and lays out a week-by-week plan with owner, hours and rep gate per action, the Data Explorer query as baseline, and the daily rotating tag-feed check.
expectations: Rejects the shared QuillbridgeSupport account: one person, one account, no shared or agency accounts; each of the 4 engineers posts from an individual account

Rejects LLM-drafted answers even with an engineer checking them, citing the ban on content crafted in part or in whole by generative AI and its penalties (deletion with its reputation, warning, suspension on repeat)
Tells engineers to debug with AI privately and write the post themselves
Rejects the 25-person upvote drive: coordinated or serial votes are reversed automatically and can suspend every account involved
States that the profile bio does not count as disclosure and that every post naming Quillbridge carries a disclosure line in the post, including the question half of a self-answered pair
Replaces oldest-first with sorting the backlog by views and ignoring the near-zero-view tail, stating that oldest-first spends the most hours on threads nobody reads
Restates the goal 'clear the backlog' as owning the high-view threads
Picks the Curate posture and states its predicate: new questions still arrive monthly and the goal is deflection
Clusters the backlog by root cause with one self-answered canonical per cluster and the remaining threads flagged as duplicates onto it
Provides or points to the Data Explorer query on data.stackexchange.com listing open questions with no upvoted or accepted answer, highest views first, as the backlog source
Handles bugs posted as questions with a workaround plus a disclosed link to the public issue, and account or billing threads with a 50+ rep steward commenting the support route and flagging to close
Gives the rep gate per action: self-answered canonical and duplicate flag at 15 rep, close vote at 3,000 rep
Carries the user's figures through unchanged: 1,412 questions, 338 unanswered, 4 engineers, 3 hours a week each, 8 weeks
Batches edits and updates weekly rather than spreading them daily, because every edit bumps the thread to the Active tab
Includes the daily 15-minute rotating check of the tag feed (/feeds/tag/quillbridge) with one assignee per question, and states the deflection goal promotes the new-question rotation

evals.prompt: Honest question. We're Tarnwick Labs, a secrets manager with a CLI, tag [tarnwick] on Stack Overflow, 212 questions total. New questions in the tag: 3 in January, 5 in February, 2 in March. The old threads still get traffic though - the top one, 'tarnwick login fails with "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority"', has 41k views and its accepted answer from 2019 tells people to set TARNWICK_SKIP_VERIFY, which we removed in v3 (the fix now is `tarnwick config set ca-bundle <path>`). I'm the only DevRel, I can give this about 90 minutes a week, no deadline. Our CTO's goal is that when someone asks ChatGPT or another AI assistant how to do something with Tarnwick, they get our answer. Should we just abandon Stack Overflow and put the time into docs, or what's the minimum worth doing? If there's something to post, write it.
evals.expected_output: A reply that picks the Maintain posture with its hours predicate, rejects Exit because questions still arrive, explains why the archive still matters for citation (licensed to Google and OpenAI, cited by AI assistants, under 1% of the 2014 peak in new questions), ranks the tag excerpt and wiki first and canonicals second, recommends a new answer on the 41k-view thread rather than an edit, delivers the answer template with the technical body left for staff, and sets self-set metrics including a monthly AI-citation spot check.
expectations: Picks the Maintain posture, states its predicate (under about 2 hours a week), and drops the daily new-question rotation, duplicate flagging and bounties from the plan
Does not recommend exiting Stack Overflow: states new questions still arrive monthly, so the Exit posture (almost no new questions) does not apply

States that monthly new questions sit under 1% of the 2014 peak while the archive still ranks in search, is licensed to Google and OpenAI, and is among domains AI assistants cite, as the reason the archive still serves the CTO's goal

Ranks surfaces by value per hour with the tag excerpt and wiki first, then self-answered canonicals, then a new answer on a high-view outdated thread, and states that the citation goal promotes canonicals
For the 41k-view x509 thread, recommends posting a new answer from the DevRel's own account rather than editing the 2019 accepted answer
States that accepted answers are no longer pinned above higher-scored ones, as published by Stack Overflow, so a correct new answer can rank above the outdated accepted one
States that rewriting another author's answer gets rolled back and that edits below 2,000 rep that change intent are rejected
Labels 'titles quoting the literal error string rank best' as practitioner reverse-engineering, unconfirmed, not a published ranking rule
Adds a monthly AI-citation spot check as a metric and states that targets are self-set because Stack Overflow publishes no vendor-tag benchmark
Gives the rep gates: tag excerpt and wiki at any rep but peer-reviewed, self-answered canonical at 15 rep, new answer at 1 rep

Delivers the x509 answer as the filled template (one-sentence direct answer, fix with the version tested, 'Why it works', disclosure line naming Tarnwick Labs and Tarnwick, reference link) with the technical body marked for staff to write, giving the generative-AI ban as the reason, rather than a post ready to paste
Keeps every proposed action inside 90 minutes a week with hours stated per action
Carries the figures through: 212 questions, 3/5/2 new questions per month, 41k views, TARNWICK_SKIP_VERIFY removed in v3

evals.prompt: Need help fast. One of our engineers at Ferrostack (Rust ORM, tag [ferrostack]) had 3 answers deleted this week and got a notice mentioning six spam flags. He's at 212 rep and his profile says 'Core engineer @ Ferrostack'. Looking at his answers: most end with 'see our migration guide: <link>' and two were only the link. Two more things on his list. On the biggest thread in our tag (18k views) the accepted answer from 2021 recommends `ferro::migrate::auto()`, which we deprecated in 0.9 - he wants to edit that answer and swap in `ferro::migrate::plan().apply()`. And on two threads an engineer from a competing ORM posted answers steering people to their product and claiming Ferrostack has no async support, which is false since 0.7 - he wants to downvote both and flag them as spam. What should he do on each of these three things?
evals.expected_output: A reply that explains the deletions (six spam flags, link-only answers, no in-post disclosure), rewrites his answer pattern with the template, warns of automatic answer bans and the some-but-not-all share, tells him to post a new answer on the 18k thread instead of editing the accepted one, and forbids downvoting or flagging the competitor's answers in favour of a new disclosed answer correcting the claim.
expectations: Explains the deletions by the enforced limit: six spam or abusive flags delete the post and cost 100 rep, and link-only answers are deleted
States that the profile line 'Core engineer @ Ferrostack' does not count as disclosure; each post naming Ferrostack needs a disclosure line in the post body
Rewrites his answer pattern with the template: one-sentence direct answer, runnable code or steps with the version tested, 'Why it works', disclosure line, docs link only as a reference at the end
Warns that downvoted, closed or deleted posts trigger automatic answer bans, and sets the hygiene target at zero further spam flags, undisclosed-affiliation comments and rejected edits
Tells him some but not all answers may be about Ferrostack, so he also answers questions where the product is not the solution
On the 18k-view thread: does not edit the 2021 accepted answer; posts a new answer with the 0.9 API instead, stating edits below 2,000 rep that change intent are rejected and rewrites get rolled back
States accepted answers are no longer pinned above higher-scored ones, so the new answer can overtake the deprecated accepted one
On the competitor's two answers: does not downvote, flag or retag them; posts a new disclosed answer correcting the async-support claim with a working example
Names the rule 'hands off others' work' (never downvote, flag or retag competitors' posts) as the reason, not just etiquette
Does not suggest colleagues vote on, accept or bounty his posts to recover reputation or ranking
Proposes one migration answer for the 0.9 deprecations as the duplicate target for other threads still using `ferro::migrate::auto()`
Carries the figures through: 212 rep, 3 deleted answers, 18k views, deprecated in 0.9, async since 0.7

evals.prompt: We get the same support ticket about 30 times a month at Larkmoor (message queue, Go SDK larkq-go, tag [larkq]): consumers crash on startup with `larkq: handshake rejected: protocol version 4 not supported by broker (max 3)` after upgrading the SDK to 2.x against an older broker. The fix is to pass `larkq.WithProtocol(3)` until the broker is on 1.14 or later. I have 230 rep. Write me the Stack Overflow Q&A for this so it's what people land on when they search the error, plus a new tag excerpt and tag wiki - the current excerpt says 'Larkmoor is the fastest open-source message queue for cloud-native teams. Get started free at larkmoor.io'. Make the answer complete so engineering doesn't have to touch it. One more thing: there's a really good community answer on an older thread about broker TLS setup that we'd love to reuse on our docs site - can we just copy it in?
evals.expected_output: A reply that first checks for an existing thread, then fills the canonical Q&A template (literal-error title, disclosure in both question and answer, Cause/Fix/Verify/Applies-to sections) with the technical body left for staff because of the generative-AI ban, rewrites the tag excerpt as neutral usage guidance and the wiki in the three-section shape, confirms the 15-rep self-answer gate, states CC BY-SA 4.0 reuse with attribution, and points the docs mirror to the troubleshooting-docs sibling.
expectations: Before posting a new Q&A, instructs searching the [larkq] tag for an existing thread on this error and answering there if one exists
Uses the canonical title shape '<tool> fails with "<literal error string>" when <condition>' with the literal `handshake rejected: protocol version 4 not supported by broker (max 3)` string
Puts a disclosure line in the question post itself, stating the Larkmoor affiliation and that the Q&A documents a common fix, not only in the answer
Puts a disclosure line in the answer post naming Larkmoor and larkq
Structures the answer as Cause, Fix, Verify, Applies to versions, carrying the 2.x SDK and broker 1.14+ ranges

Leaves the technical body (code block, verify command and expected output) for staff to write and states the reason: content crafted in part by generative AI is banned; does not deliver a 'complete' answer body despite the request
Instructs ticking 'Answer your own question' on the Ask page and confirms the 15-rep gate is met at 230 rep

Rewrites the tag excerpt as neutral usage guidance (one-line definition, use for questions about using larkq, bugs/feature requests/account issues to Larkmoor's own channels), removing 'fastest', 'Get started free' and the marketing link
Writes the tag wiki with About, Before asking (versions and full error output, links to canonicals) and Where else to ask (bug, feature request, account URLs) sections
States the tag excerpt and wiki edits are peer-reviewed and carry no rep gate
States posts are CC BY-SA 4.0, so the community TLS answer may be reused on the docs site with attribution
Points the mirrored docs error page to the developer-troubleshooting-docs sibling skill rather than writing the docs page inline
Treats the 30-a-month ticket theme as one of the quarterly 5-10 canonicals for top support-ticket themes and names duplicate flags (15 rep) onto it for existing threads
Carries the figures through: 30 tickets a month, 230 rep, protocol 4 vs max 3, broker 1.14+, SDK 2.x, larkq.WithProtocol(3)

evals.prompt: First week as developer advocate at Vexalith (feature flags, SDKs vexa-js and vexa-py, tag [vexalith]). I created my Stack Overflow account yesterday, 1 rep. The tag has 96 open questions. About a third are 'is this a bug?' posts with stack traces, several are billing complaints ('charged twice for seats'), one asks 'Flagbeam vs Vexalith vs Togglewright - which should I pick for a Django app', and three are on pt.stackoverflow.com in a [vexalith] tag there, in Portuguese. My plan: close the billing and bug ones so the tag looks clean, answer the comparison one since it's an easy win for us, reply to the Portuguese ones in English because my Portuguese is bad, and set something up so we see new questions the same day. I have about 4 hours a week and a colleague, Dario, has an old account with 640 rep. Where do I start?
evals.expected_output: A reply that starts the 1-rep account answering at once, lists the rep gates that block closing and commenting, routes bug reports to workaround-plus-issue-link answers rather than closure, hands billing threads to the 640-rep colleague as steward, declines the tool-comparison question as off-topic, answers the Portuguese threads in Portuguese, delivers the week-1 routing table, sets up the daily tag-feed rotation, and sizes the plan to 4 hours a week.
expectations: States that answering needs no reputation and starts the advocate answering in the [vexalith] tag from the 1-rep account in week 1
Lists the gates that block the plan as written: comment at 50 rep, flag at 15, close vote at 3,000; the new account cannot close or comment yet
Does not close the bug reports; answers each with a workaround plus a disclosed link to the public issue, using the bug-report redirect wording
Assigns the billing threads to Dario (640 rep, above the 50-rep steward gate) to comment the support route and flag to close as not about programming, with the '(I work at Vexalith.)' line

Declines to answer the 'which should I pick' question on Stack Overflow because tool recommendations are off-topic there; notes Software Recommendations accepts such a question only when the answer meets every stated requirement
Answers the three Portuguese threads in Portuguese on pt.stackoverflow.com (a separate tag), never in English; hands them to a Portuguese speaker if needed
States reputation is per site and that 200 rep on any Stack Exchange site adds 100 on every other
Delivers the week-1 routing table: how-to and error questions to Stack Overflow; bugs, feature requests, 'why' and 'when' questions to Vexalith's own channels, on the support page and the tag excerpt
Sets up the daily 15-minute rotating check from the tag feed (/feeds/tag/vexalith) into chat with one assignee per question, plus a weekly 1-2 hour steward slot
Sorts the 96 open questions by views and ignores the near-zero-view tail before any work, rather than working the whole list to make the tag look clean
Sets the metric baseline: answer rate under 30 days starting at 90% and median time to first answer of one business day, or supplies the Data Explorer query to compute it
Keeps the plan inside 4 hours a week with hours per action and the rep gate stated per action

evals.prompt: Our VP Eng at Brindlecore (time-series database, tag [brindledb]) wants a quarterly Stack Overflow slide. She asked for three things: (a) our answer rate against the industry benchmark for vendor tags, (b) total team reputation as the headline KPI with a target of +5,000 per quarter, and (c) 'questions edited or cleaned up' as the activity metric, since the two engineers answering (both around 1,800 rep) spend a lot of time tidying old posts. I need the actual numbers from Stack Exchange data. Give me the exact query and the metrics to put on the slide.
evals.expected_output: A reply that refuses to invent a benchmark (targets are self-set), replaces reputation and edit counts with the skill's metric set (answer rate under 30 days, time to first answer, canonical coverage, canonical views, AI-citation spot check, hygiene at zero), explains why edits are a cost not an activity metric, and supplies the exact Data Explorer query with the 30-day answer-rate variant.
expectations: States that Stack Overflow publishes no vendor-tag benchmark and that targets are self-set; supplies no industry benchmark answer rate
Proposes answer rate under 30 days with a self-set starting target of 90% and median time to first answer of one business day
Does not adopt total team reputation or the +5,000 per quarter target as a KPI
Rejects 'questions edited or cleaned up' as a metric, stating every edit bumps the thread to the Active tab and that edits are batched weekly
Adds hygiene with pass threshold zero: spam flags, AI deletions, undisclosed-affiliation comments, rejected edits
Adds canonical coverage of the top 20 support-ticket themes, views on canonicals, and a monthly AI-citation spot check

Provides the Data Explorer query for data.stackexchange.com with the exact filters: PostTypeId = 1, ClosedDate IS NULL, AcceptedAnswerId IS NULL, NOT EXISTS an answer with Score > 0, ORDER BY ViewCount DESC, parameterized with ##TagName:string##

For the answer-rate metric, adds the 30-day window (CreationDate > DATEADD(day, -30, GETDATE())) and compares against all open questions in the same window with the same ClosedDate IS NULL filter on both sides
States the Data Explorer database refreshes weekly
Notes the two engineers at about 1,800 rep sit below the 2,000-rep unreviewed-edit gate, so their edits are reviewed and intent-changing edits get rejected and count against hygiene
Carries the figures through: two engineers at about 1,800 rep, quarterly cadence
Opens with direct answers to the three asks before the query and metric list

evals.prompt: Oakhollow (payments API, SDK oakhollow-node, tag [oakhollow]). Our senior engineer Priya just passed 3,100 rep so she can finally close things. The tag has about 80 questions that are all the same 'webhook signature mismatch' problem in slightly different wording, and roughly half are on our v1 SDK, which we sunset last year. Plan: Priya closes all 80 as duplicates of our new canonical over one weekend and edits each one to add a line pointing to the canonical. We also got $2,000 of community budget approved - I want to put 100-200 rep bounties on the 15 hardest open questions in the tag to pull in outside answerers. And since Stack Overflow has Collectives, should we start an Oakhollow Collective so we have our own space? Sanity-check the plan.
evals.expected_output: A reply that corrects the close-vote assumption (one of three votes; only a gold tag badge closes alone; colleagues never supply the rest), replaces per-question edits with duplicate flags that the site comments on itself, splits the sunset v1 half onto a migration answer, explains bounties come from the poster's own reputation and rank last, and declines a new Collective under the join-only-if-one-exists rule.
expectations: States that at 3,100 rep Priya's close vote is one of three, and that only a gold tag badge (1,000 tag score and 200 answers in the tag) closes duplicates alone
States that colleagues never supply the other close votes, because coordinated votes are reversed and can suspend every account involved
Recommends badge-building toward the gold tag badge because most of the backlog is repeats
Replaces the per-question edits with duplicate flags or votes onto the canonical, stating the site posts the link comment itself; a staff comment is added only to point at the version-specific part
Warns that every edit bumps the thread to the Active tab, so 80 edits in one weekend is a bulk-edit pattern; batches work weekly
Splits the sunset v1 half: one migration answer as the duplicate target for the v1 threads, separate from the current canonical
States a bounty is paid from the poster's own reputation (75-rep gate), so the $2,000 budget cannot fund bounties
Ranks bounty last in value per hour as a one-shot surface, below canonicals and duplicate flags
Does not recommend starting an Oakhollow Collective; states the rule: join a Collective only if your technology already has one
Does not paste the canonical's answer onto the 80 threads; flags them as duplicates instead
Gives the rep gates: duplicate flag at 15, duplicate vote at 3,000
Ensures the new canonical carries a disclosure line in both the question and the answer post
Carries the figures through: about 80 questions, 3,100 rep, 15 questions, $2,000, v1 sunset
